# `redundant-boolean-negation`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports double boolean negation operations (`!!x` or `!(!x)`) and negated
boolean constants (`!true` or `!false`).
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

In Zig, the `!` operator only accepts boolean values, so double negation is
always a no-op that produces the original boolean value. Negating literal `true`
or `false` is always equivalent to using the opposite constant directly. In
languages like C or JavaScript, `!!x` is used to cast integers or pointers to
booleans, but in Zig that idiom is invalid or redundant.

## When it fires

It applies to double boolean negation expressions and negated boolean constants,
offering a quickfix to use the simplified operand directly.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn isReady(flag: bool) bool {
    return !!flag;
}
```
